notable_absence.finding: No Prerequisites section on this page at all, same absence pattern as WHERE and unlike WITH (its non-recursive sibling) - WITH RECURSIVE's own docs page states no privilege requirement, presumably because it inherits the same read privilege as WITH/SELECT without restating it. Also no requiresEdition/availableSince at the page-intro level (unlike window.md/windowfun.md); the only version citation on this page is scoped to a single error-message detail (see cross_product_finding), not a feature-availability gate.

cross_component_finding: This page documents two concrete implicit resource limits with hard numeric defaults - 'Exceeding the implicit document limit (10000) when a memory quota is not in use...' and 'Exceeding the implicit level limit (1000) when the level option is not in use...' - which is a level of quantitative specificity not seen elsewhere in this batch's clause-reference pages. Flagged for visibility even though no relation predicate was minted for it, since these constants (10000 documents / 1000 levels) look like durable, checkable facts a future ontology round may want a dedicated 'hasImplicitLimit' predicate for.
cross_product_finding: Recurrence of the known issue in docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json: 'Couchbase Server 7.6.2' is cited as a version heading directly above an example error message ('In Couchbase Server 7.6.2, the CYCLE clause returns the following error if you enter an invalid expression'), despite Capella having no discrete version numbers. Narrower than window.md/windowfun.md's edition+feature-availability citations - this one gates a specific error-message wording/error-code detail rather than a language capability.
